title: Mutable bindings and &mut
summary: mut on a binding allows change; &mut lends exclusive write access — one writer at a time.
lecture: Bindings are immutable unless declared `let mut`. A `&mut T` reference lends the right to modify — and it is exclusive: while a mutable borrow lives, no other borrow of that value may exist, shared or mutable.

The borrow checker enforces one-writer-XOR-many-readers at compile time. E0499 (two mutable borrows) and E0502 (mutable plus shared borrow) are its signatures — and the usual fix is not cleverness but ORDER: finish reading before you write, or write before you hand out views.
Non-lexical lifetimes help you: a borrow ends at its last use, not at the closing brace, so reordering statements is often the entire fix.

example.code:
let mut score = String::from("10");
let preview = &score;      // shared borrow…
println!("was {preview}"); // …last use here
score.push('0');           // now mutation is fine
example.caption: Read first, then mutate — the borrow has already ended.
